code: file <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt") writeLines(c(1, 8, 80, 2, 1, 20, 0, "&", 15, 8, 8, 20, 10, 2, 0, "&",              15, 81, 80, 2, 1, 2, 0), file)  x <- scan(file, what = "", quiet = TRUE) samples <- unname(split(as.numeric(x[x != "&"]), cumsum(x == "&")[x != "&"])) do.call(rbind, lapply(samples, function(y) {   fit <- suppressWarnings(optim_etienne(y))   data.frame(S = length(y[y > 0]), J = sum(y), theta = fit$theta, se_theta = fit$se_theta,              m = fit$m, se_m = fit$se_m,              negloglik = -logl_etienne(y, fit$theta, fit$m, full = TRUE),              n_local_maxima = nrow(fit$local_maxima)) })) #>   S   J     theta   se_theta           m        se_m negloglik n_local_maxima #> 1 6 112  1.195285         NA 0.999999990          NA  10.77968              2 #> 2 6  63  2.947770   2.582702 0.102035222 0.120382867  12.22751              1 #> 3 6 181 21.747365 110.037756 0.006867291 0.006534417  13.53646              2 optim_multideme(do.call(rbind, samples), ci = TRUE)[c("I", "se_I", "m", "se_m", "ci_m")] #> $I #> [1]  7.419698  5.738001 14.671141 #>  #> $se_I #> [1] 4.337811 3.235172 9.373103 #>  #> $m #> [1] 0.06265594 0.08470874 0.07536372 #>  #> $se_m #> [1] 0.03433568 0.04371438 0.04451975 #>  #> $ci_m #>           lower     upper #> [1,] 0.01858430 0.1636401 #> [2,] 0.02650112 0.2057232 #> [3,] 0.02043186 0.2125176 y <- samples[[2]] fit <- optim_etienne(y) lk <- logkda(y)                                  # computed once for the whole grid grid <- expand.grid(theta = exp(seq(log(0.5), log(200), length.out = 80)),                     m = seq(0.005, 1, length.out = 80)) grid$logl <- logl_etienne(y, grid$theta, grid$m, log_kda = lk) z <- matrix(grid$logl - fit$logl, 80, 80) image(log(unique(grid$theta)), unique(grid$m), pmax(z, -10), col = hcl.colors(50),       xlab = "log(theta)", ylab = "m") contour(log(unique(grid$theta)), unique(grid$m), z, levels = -qchisq(0.95, 2) / 2,         drawlabels = FALSE, add = TRUE) points(log(fit$theta), fit$m, pch = 19)

code: library(neutr)  # Generate a community: Ewens model, theta = 11.3, 234,373 individuals set.seed(1) com <- generate_hoppe_urn(theta = 11.3, J = 234373) length(com$abundance)      # number of species in this draw (expected: com$k)  # Estimate the parameters ab <- c(234, 87, 34, 5, 4, 3, 3, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1) ew <- optim_ewens(ab)                        # Ewens theta pm <- optim_pitman(ab, c(10, 0.1))           # Pitman theta and sigma  # Compare the nested models (Ewens is Pitman with sigma = 0): the log-likelihoods are comparable 2 * (pm$logl - ew$logl)                      # likelihood-ratio statistic  # Etienne model: a local community with dispersal limitation (Ewens is Etienne with m = 1) et <- optim_etienne(c(8, 5, 3, 2, 1, 1))     # theta = 7.05, m = 0.226 (Etienne 2005)  # Multideme model: one row per deme, one column per species optim_multideme(rbind(c(44, 37, 34, 5, 4, 3, 3, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1),                       c(240, 20, 48, 2, 21, 1, 3, 2, 5, 2, 0, 1, 1)))

title: Etienne's coefficients \(K(D,A)\) of the sampling formula with dispersal limitation — logkda
text: logkda() computes logarithm coefficients \(K(D,)\) Etienne's sampling formula (Etienne 2005, equation A11), species abundance distribution \(D = (n_1, ..., n_k)\) \(\) k \(J=\sum n_i\). coefficients depend data , parameters, expensive part logl_etienne() optim_etienne(). \(K(D,)\) coefficient \(x^\) polynomial \(\prod_{=1}^k T_{n_i}(x)\), \(T_n(x)=\sum_a T_n[] x^\) \(T_1[1]=1\) \(T_n[] = T_{n-1}[] + T_{n-1}[-1](-1)/(n-1)\), .e. \(T_n[] = |s(n,)|(-1)!/(n-1)!\) \(s\) Stirling numbers first kind. recursion polynomial products evaluated entirely log scale, calculation overflow whatever sample size.

title: Log-likelihood of Etienne's sampling formula — logl_etienne
text: logl_etienne() computes log-likelihood Etienne's sampling formula species abundance distribution \((n_1, ..., n_k)\), given fundamental biodiversity number \(\theta\) metacommunity immigration rate \(m\) local community. rescaled immigration rate \(=\frac{m}{1-m}(J-1)\) \(J=\sum n_i\), log-likelihood $$k\log\theta + \log\Gamma(\theta) + \sum_i\log\Gamma(n_i)   + \log\Gamma() - \log\Gamma(+J)   + \log\sum_{=k}^{J} K(D,)\frac{^}{\Gamma(\theta+)}$$ \(K(D,)\) given logkda(). function vectorised theta m.

title: neutr 0.2.0
text: New optim.etienne(): maximum likelihood estimation fundamental biodiversity number theta immigration rate m Etienne’s (2005) sampling formula, local community dispersal limitation. likelihood surface can multimodal: profiled parameters refined stats::optim(method = "L-BFGS-B") exact gradient. Returns theta, m, , logl converged, warns estimate lies edge search interval (m, upper bound means evidence dispersal limitation). optim.etienne() returns standard errors (se_theta, se_m, se_I, inverse Hessian), distinct local maxima found (local_maxima, TeTame reports second maximum), ci = TRUE likelihood-ratio confidence intervals (ci_theta, ci_m, ci_I). New logl.etienne(): log-likelihood Etienne’s sampling formula, vectorised theta m. scale logl optim.ewens() optim.pitman(); m = 1 equals Ewens log-likelihood, Ewens model nested Etienne model. full = TRUE gives probability species abundance distribution . optim.multideme() returns standard errors m (se_I, se_m, exact curvature likelihood) , ci = TRUE, likelihood-ratio confidence intervals (ci_I, ci_m). replace Std_I Std_m columns TeTame, whose curvature lacks factor 0.01 . additions, neutr covers functionality TeTame 2.1 software (Chave Jabot): see vignette reading TeTame data files plotting likelihood surface. New logkda(): coefficients K(D,) formula, computed entirely log scale. code comes package untb (R. K. S. Hankin), replaces earlier implementations required PARI/GP packages Brobdingnag, partitions polynom: neutr gains new dependency. Results agree PARI/GP 1e-15.

title: neutr 0.1.1
text: optim.ewens() optim.pitman() return log-likelihood (logl) scale (log-probability partition), Ewens model, Pitman model sigma = 0, can compared directly Pitman model likelihood ratio AIC. optim.ewens() solves score equation k = theta (digamma(theta + J) - digamma(theta)) directly, full numerical precision. optim.pitman() maximises likelihood stats::optim(method = "L-BFGS-B") exact gradient, two starting points. New arguments lower upper set search interval, result converged element. optim.multideme() scans deme likelihood log grid refining maximum. New logl element result, new verbose I_max arguments; data frame counts accepted. deme single individual NA immigration rate (warning). estimators warn estimate lies edge search interval, .e. likelihood interior maximum data.
